# **Architectural Framework for Strong-Model Oversight of Local Agentic Orchestrators**

## **Theoretical Foundations and Empirical Evidence in Agent Supervision**

Scalable oversight addresses the governance challenge of maintaining alignment, correctness, and execution integrity in autonomous language agents when problem spaces are expansive and supervisory compute is constrained1. In autonomous software engineering, running an elite frontier model such as Claude Opus as a persistent, turn-by-turn orchestrator across hundreds of interaction steps is economically unviable3. As a result, contemporary agent architectures partition responsibilities: a localized, low-cost model, such as an open-weight Qwen 3.x-class agent, executes tool calls, manages context, and delegates granular subtasks, while an external frontier model is invoked intermittently as a specialized overseer3.  
The literature on strong-to-weak supervision and critic-driven oversight demonstrates that code synthesis benefits from structural asymmetries absent in open-ended creative writing1. In code spaces, verifying an execution trajectory or validating an architectural diff requires substantially less generation compute than synthesizing the original solution or performing broad repository search2. Early foundations in automated code review, marked by OpenAI’s CriticGPT in July 2024, established that reinforcement learning from human feedback (RLHF) tuned for critique could detect bugs that human contractors missed across 63% of comparative evaluations6. CriticGPT proved that dedicated critic models catch subtle semantic bugs and reduce hallucinated criticisms7. However, its architecture was optimized as an offline human-assistance tool rather than an active, real-time intervention engine within an autonomous agentic loop8.  
Recent research focuses on runtime supervision where the critic actively steers frozen or resource-constrained coding agents3. Gandhi et al. (June 2026\) demonstrated that deploying small and large critic models over frozen software engineering agents on SWE-bench Verified yielded absolute resolution rate improvements between 5.6 and 16.0 percentage points across six different underlying agent models3. Significantly, their findings established that high-level strategic supervision consistently outperformed low-level, command-by-command code corrections3. For instance, on Qwen3-Next-80B-A3B, high-level steering achieved a 25.2% resolve rate compared to 24.6% for granular instructions, while cutting total operational costs by a factor of 5.2 to 6.03.  
The structural breakthrough in late-2026 agent oversight was formalized in the Opera framework by Mei et al. (October 2026\)9. Opera treats verbal criticism not as fleeting context injection, but as the management of persistent corrective notes governed by admission and release audits9. Across extensive evaluations on Terminal-Bench 2.1, SWE-bench Pro, and DeepSWE v1.1, Opera elevated resolve rates by up to 15.0 percentage points on SWE-bench Pro when paired with a Qwen3.5-9B policy model, and by 8.9 percentage points on DeepSWE v1.1 when paired with Qwen3.8-27B4. These results confirm that strong-model oversight functions as a forceful capability multiplier when the baseline model has sufficient domain competence to parse and execute tactical redirects3. Nevertheless, DeepSWE evaluations reveal a definitive capability boundary: when a policy agent possesses near-zero baseline capability on deeply complex tasks, external critic intervention cannot compensate for the underlying deficit in software engineering reasoning4.

The qualitative findings of these benchmarks indicate that the primary utility of a strong model is not synthesizing routine code, but suppressing search-space explosion3. Weaker local orchestrators routinely succumb to local optima, pursuing superficial patches that mask underlying algorithmic regressions12. A strong model acts as an epistemic anchor, forcing the local orchestrator to reconcile intermediate implementations against broader system specifications and global repository contracts2.

## **Quantitative Return-on-Investment of Oversight Trigger Events**

Invoking Claude Opus on every agent turn rapidly exhausts token budgets without yielding proportional quality improvements3. Fixed-interval periodic review, which calls an overseer every ![][image2] turns, exhibits severe efficiency defects: it reacts slowly to immediate tactical errors, allowing the agent to repeat failing commands multiple times before intervention, while squandering expensive tokens reviewing benign file reads and exploratory shell commands4. Conversely, reviewing work exclusively at the conclusion of a session exposes the system to catastrophic sunk-cost cascades, where an erroneous assumption made on turn three invalidates forty subsequent turns of complex implementation12.  
The optimal supervisory posture balances event-driven interventions with deterministic, zero-cost tripwires9. By evaluating the empirical yield of distinct triggering events across recent software engineering benchmarks, triggers can be ranked based on their defect-prevention yield relative to the overseer token expenditure incurred.

| Rank | Trigger Event | Trigger Category | Primary Vulnerability Addressed | Quality Yield per Oversight Call | Cost Impact per Call | Recommended Harness Action |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| **1** | **Pre-Commit Task Completion Claim** | Deterministic State Gate | Premature exit, silent regression, unhandled edge cases, missing test verification | Highest: catches 40–60% of false-positive completions before trunk contamination9 | Moderate (Plan \+ Full Diff \+ Test Logs) | **Binding Gate**: Blocks final commit tool until the overseer emits an explicit approval token22. |
| **2** | **Consecutive Check or Test Failure** | State Transition Tripwire | Flawed hypothesis loop, localized regression, assertion thrashing, wrong repair locus | High: resolves stalled debugging cycles in \~70% of multi-turn repair attempts4 | Low-to-Moderate (Stderr \+ Focal Diff \+ Strategy State) | **Advisory Steering**: Overseer injects high-level diagnostic guidance; resets worker trajectory3. |
| **3** | **High-Risk Domain Interception** | Static AST / File Pattern Match | Schema destruction, security regression, public interface breakage, race conditions | Critical Safety: prevents catastrophic production outages and contract drift23 | Moderate (Spec \+ Target Schema/Interface \+ Proposed Diff) | **Binding Authorization**: Halts execution; requires structural overseer sign-off to proceed22. |
| **4** | **Plan Inception / Architectural Spec** | Lifecycle Milestone | Problem misinterpretation, improper component localization, architectural hallucination | High Preventive: improves downstream resolution by up to 20% on complex tasks14 | Low (Issue description \+ Initial plan draft \+ Repo summary) | **Advisory Steering**: Validates technical direction before file write operations begin14. |
| **5** | **Semantic Stalling / Circular Looping** | Algorithmic Heuristic Trigger | Oscillatory edits, infinite execution loops, unprogressed token consumption | Moderate: breaks terminal agent loops where rule-based breaks fail9 | Low (Action history hashes \+ Stagnant context delta) | **Binding Rollback**: Forces trajectory rewind to last known stable checkpoint22. |

The trade-offs between plan-level verification and diff-level verification represent fundamentally distinct points on the risk-cost spectrum19. Plan review, as evaluated in workflows like Research-Plan-Implement (RPI) and CodeScout (March 2026), provides high preventive leverage: correcting an orchestrator's initial mental model and file localization before code is written eliminates dozens of downstream refactoring turns14. However, plan verification alone cannot verify implementation fidelity, as local orchestrators frequently drift from approved plans or introduce low-level syntactic and concurrency defects during code generation24. Consequently, pre-commit diff review offers the single highest defect-interception return on investment, acting as an uncompromising quality barrier against silent functional failures19.  
Event-triggered reviews outshine periodic reviews in token efficiency by aligning overseer invocations directly with state entropy changes9. Rather than interrogating the agent at arbitrary clock cycles, event triggers fire precisely when the local orchestrator experiences an impasse—such as consecutive test failures—or attempts an irreversible operation9. As demonstrated in the Opera ablation studies, pairing immediate event triggers with a sparse periodic fallback prevents the overseer from missing silent drifts (such as an agent modifying the wrong codebase subsystem without generating test errors) while preserving a lean token budget4.

## **Context Packaging and Token Economics for Asymmetric Oversight**

A recurring architectural failure in multi-agent implementations is streaming the entire raw session transcript into the overseer's context window18. Raw transcripts contain immense operational noise, including repetitive directory listings, verbose compiler outputs, and discarded intermediate edits32. Exposing a frontier model to unabridged context not only inflates API costs exponentially, but also degrades diagnostic precision due to context saturation and "lost-in-the-middle" attention dispersion32.  
Empirical literature on context compaction reveals both the necessity and the hazards of trajectory condensation32. Studies evaluating AutoCompact (October 2026\) and CompactionRL (July 2026\) show that replacing stale history with concise working state improves long-horizon task completion across SWE-bench Verified and Terminal-Bench33. Outcome-based reinforcement learning reduces key-state omissions in agent summaries from 3.1% to 0.2%33. However, findings from Compact-Bench (arXiv:2610.31710, late 2026\) document the "Compaction Cliff," revealing that general-purpose language model summarizers retain at most 16% of recurring execution details and frequently discard crucial environment flags, mock parameters, and localized syntax constraints32.  
To optimize both cost and detection fidelity, the overseer must receive a strictly structured, trigger-specific payload prepared by the deterministic harness rather than an opaque, lossy narrative summary10.

| Trigger Event | Payload Components Provided to Overseer | Explicitly Omitted Context | Token Budget Range | Target Detection Objective |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| **Pre-Commit Task Completion** | Task specification; complete unified git diff (git diff main...HEAD); AST symbol table delta; comprehensive test execution matrix. | Granular bash command histories; exploratory file reads; superseded intermediate patches. | 4,000 – 12,000 tokens | Verify requirement satisfaction; check for regressions; detect missing edge-case coverage9. |
| **Consecutive Test Failure** | Target test source code; last two stderr traces; localized diff of modules under test; agent’s stated working hypothesis. | Global repository file tree; unrelated terminal outputs; successful background test logs. | 2,000 – 5,000 tokens | Identify flawed diagnostic logic; detect circular repair attempts; redirect search locus3. |
| **High-Risk Domain Interception** | Target interface/schema definition; proposed unified diff; static dependency call graph; explicit safety/migration policy document. | Orchestrator reasoning history; general codebase files; prior non-breaking tool executions. | 3,000 – 6,000 tokens | Enforce schema backward compatibility; verify credential/auth security; check concurrency locking23. |
| **Plan Inception** | Problem description; repository structure map (depth 2); key target signatures; agent’s candidate task breakdown and test plan. | Full implementation files; package lockfiles; external documentation text. | 3,000 – 8,000 tokens | Validate localization of fault; detect scope creep; ensure planned verification strategy is viable14. |
| **Semantic Stalling / Looping** | Action hash timeline; last 3 distinct tool calls with error returns; working tree status; git delta between turn ![][image3] and ![][image4]. | Long-tail conversational turns; historical plan iterations; verbose standard output. | 1,500 – 3,500 tokens | Determine structural root of impasse (e.g., locked files, unmocked network call); issue escape command26. |

Engineering this context assembly requires strict deterministic pre-filtering19. The system harness strips standard output lines exceeding fixed bounds, preserving only exception headers and the terminal segments of stack traces18. By prioritizing unified git diffs and structured test matrices over conversational history, the harness provides the overseer with objective, authoritative state rather than the local agent's subjective account of its progress17.

## **Governance Architecture: Advisory Steering versus Binding Structural Enforcement**

A critical design choice in multi-agent orchestration is determining whether an overseer’s output functions as an advisory suggestion or a binding command22. In early agentic configurations, supervisors operated conversationally, offering polite recommendations that the worker agent could interpret flexibly22. Empirical evidence reveals that this advisory model breaks down when applied to weaker open-weight orchestrators22.  
Weaker models suffer from documented compliance failures when processing advisory critique12. As demonstrated in the comparative analysis of the PEVR and EVA multi-agent frameworks (arXiv:2605.30102, May 2026), structured replanning signals consistently outmatched open-ended advisory feedback in stateful environments where incorrect intermediate actions produce irreversible side effects37. Weaker models routinely display conversational sycophancy: an agent politely validates the supervisor's critique ("I understand the issue with the boundary condition and will fix it immediately"), but then executes the identical failing tool invocation in the subsequent turn22. Furthermore, smaller models display an adherence-resolution disconnect12. As observed in the Opera ablation studies, a weaker agent frequently exhibits nominal adherence by adding an advised conditional check, but places it improperly within the call stack or fails to adjust dependent variables, leaving the underlying defect completely unresolved12.  
To establish behavioral reliability, system architectures must transition to mechanical boundary enforcement, as demonstrated by the Liza architecture (2026)22. In a mechanical architecture, behavioral constraints are enforced not through prompt persuasion, but through deterministic harness code and structural role separation22.

| Governance Dimension | Advisory Configuration | Binding Mechanical Architecture |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| **Enforcement Mechanism** | Prompt-injected recommendations within conversational context22. | Deterministic runtime gates and tool-level authorization policies22. |
| **Worker Response to Rejection** | Orchestrator can bypass suggestions and proceed to commit22. | Orchestrator is physically blocked from completing the task or merging code22. |
| **Overseer Output Structure** | Free-form natural language advice and code blocks3. | Strict JSON schemas specifying typed operators and explicit criteria12. |
| **Tracking of Feedback** | Stateless: critic forgets advice on subsequent interaction turns10. | Stateful: persistent note remains open until release audit passes10. |
| **Cost Profile** | High churn: weak agent repeatedly misinterprets advice12. | High leverage: forces immediate trajectory correction or halts session3. |

Under a binding architecture, the local worker orchestrator lacks the structural authority to mark its own work complete22. The tool allowing task resolution or repository integration is physically isolated from the local agent and resides solely within the harness environment, accessible only upon receipt of an explicit approval token from Claude Opus22. When the overseer issues a rejection, the harness rejects the worker's completion claim and injects the overseer's diagnosis into the worker's execution loop as a mandatory objective12.  
To prevent the overseer from overstepping its supervisory role and attempting to write the full implementation itself—which inflates output token generation costs by an order of magnitude—the system must impose strict tool and schema invariants3. Claude Opus must have zero access to environment write tools3. It operates as a detached diagnostic engine whose output is restricted by strict JSON schemas38. Following the Opera design, the overseer's responses must be restricted to typed operators across defined software repair phases, such as localization redirects, architectural requirement reminders, or invariant verification directives12. Enforcing this "steer, don't solve" policy preserves token efficiency while maintaining the division of labor between edge execution and centralized oversight3.

## **Zero-Cost Deterministic Signals for Pre-Overseer Loop and Failure Detection**

Invoking Claude Opus to determine whether a local agent is stuck in an infinite loop squanders expensive frontier compute on trivial state-matching problems18. Agent loops, execution stalls, and repetitive command thrashing exhibit deterministic mathematical signatures across terminal tool calls and git working trees27. These pathologies can be identified with zero model latency using lightweight, algorithmic tripwires embedded in the orchestrator harness39.  
A primary signal of agent distress is exact action repetition, which occurs when an orchestrator invokes identical tool calls with matching arguments in rapid succession27. This behavior can be tracked by maintaining a rolling FIFO queue of action hashes computed via cryptographic hashing over the normalized tool name and input parameter JSON string40. When three consecutive hashes match, an exact execution loop is flagged26. A secondary, more subtle pathology is null-state thrashing, where the agent alters files, runs build commands, and generates verbose internal reasoning, but leaves the underlying repository completely unchanged22. This failure mode is detected by hashing the git working tree across turns: if an agent executes four write operations yet the git tree hash remains identical to the prior state, the agent is oscillating or repeatedly reverting its edits27.

| Failure Signal | Detection Mechanism | Mathematical / Algorithmic Metric | Trigger Threshold | Deterministic Harness Intervention |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| **Exact Tool Loop** | Rolling cryptographic tool call hashing27. | ![][image5]; evaluate ![][image6]. | 3 identical consecutive calls. | Intercept tool; return harness error: "Identical command repeated; modify parameters or approach."26 |
| **Null-State Thrashing** | Git working tree hash comparison22. | ![][image7]; track over window. | 4 write turns with net zero tree change. | Revert unstaged changes; inject notification: "File edits produced zero net state change."27 |
| **Oscillatory Ping-Pong** | Cyclic sequence matching across recent action history17. | Subsequence repetition matching (e.g., ![][image8]) in sliding window ![][image9]. | 2 full repetitive cycles detected. | Force rollback to checkpoint preceding pattern; wipe failing hypothesis from context buffer. |
| **Diagnostic Stagnation** | Error log similarity metrics (Normalized Levenshtein)40. | ![][image10] following code edit operations. | 2 consecutive identical error traces. | Escalate to **Consecutive Test Failure Gate**; invoke Claude Opus with targeted triage payload4. |
| **Monotonic Context Bloat** | Context window consumption relative to test advancement18. | Token utilization ![][image11] of maximum context limit with 0 passing tests across ![][image12] turns. | Capacity threshold breached. | Force **AutoCompact** memory reorganization33; if stall continues, terminate session. |

Diagnostic stagnation presents another indicator of failure40. When an agent modifies source code in response to a failed compiler check or test suite, but the resulting stderr output exhibits a Normalized Levenshtein similarity or Jaccard token overlap exceeding 90%, the agent's edits are failing to engage with the error's root cause40. By catching this pattern at turn two, the harness avoids five additional turns of futile patching and triggers the overseer specifically when external diagnostic insight is required4.  
Similarly, monotonic context bloat—measured as the ratio between context window consumption and validated test milestones—provides an early warning of session exhaustion18. An orchestrator that has consumed 85% of its available context across 25 turns without establishing a single passing test assertion is engaged in unguided search33. Deterministic harness logic intercepts the agent at this boundary, executing a proactive compaction step before evaluating whether to summon frontier oversight33.

## **System Blueprint and Known Failure Modes**

Synthesizing empirical findings into an integrated architecture yields an operational blueprint for overseeing a local Qwen 3.x orchestrator with Claude Opus. The architecture organizes execution into a three-tiered hierarchy: the Deterministic Harness Layer, the Local Execution Layer, and the Frontier Governance Layer.

| Operational Phase | Primary Entity | Execution Role | Governance Authority | Phase Transition Criteria |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| **1\. Inception & Scoping** | Qwen 3.x Orchestrator | Explores codebase; decomposes task; drafts implementation plan and test specification14. | Autonomous exploration | Emits structured plan artifact to harness14. |
| **2\. Architectural Gate** | Claude Opus Overseer | Audits proposed plan, target file localization, and validation strategy14. | Advisory Steering | Plan confirmed or strategic redirect injected3. |
| **3\. Implementation Loop** | Qwen 3.x Orchestrator | Modifies code; executes local test runners; iterates against compiler outputs3. | Regulated by deterministic tripwires22 | Tests run; harness updates state metrics17. |
| **4\. Interception Tripwires** | Deterministic Harness | Monitors tool hashes, git deltas, stderr similarities, and high-risk file patterns23. | Binding Interception | Freezes execution and escalates upon tripwire breach22. |
| **5\. Pre-Commit Verification** | Claude Opus Overseer | Audits unified diff, test matrices, and task acceptance criteria9. | **Binding Gate** | Overseer emits approval token; unlocks commit tool22. |

During the initial Inception and Scoping phase, the local Qwen 3.x orchestrator reads the task statement, navigates the file tree, and drafts an implementation plan alongside an explicit testing strategy14. If the task involves high architectural complexity or ambiguous requirements, Trigger 4 summons Claude Opus to perform plan verification14. Opus reviews the proposed file touchpoints and testing plan, redirecting the local agent if it has misidentified the primary fault locus3.  
Once implementation begins, Qwen 3.x works within a containerized environment, executing shell and edit tools while the deterministic harness tracks action metrics3. If a test fails twice consecutively with identical stderr signatures, the harness triggers the Double Fault gate, pausing the orchestrator and routing the failure package to Claude Opus4. Opus diagnoses the failure and returns a typed strategy redirect, which the harness injects into Qwen's context3.  
If Qwen attempts an edit targeting high-risk boundaries—such as database schema migrations, cryptographic authentication logic, or shared public interfaces—the harness blocks the file modification and triggers the High-Risk Interception gate23. Claude Opus evaluates the safety profile and backward compatibility of the proposed change; only upon explicit validation does the harness apply the patch22.  
Finally, when Qwen asserts task completion, the harness intercepts the call, generates a complete unified diff, runs the local test suite, and presents the Task Completion package to Claude Opus9. Claude Opus performs a binding audit against the original task specification9. If defects or omissions are found, Opus issues a structured rejection with specific completion criteria, forcing the local orchestrator to resume work9. Only when Opus outputs an approval token does the harness commit the changes to the repository22.  
Deploying this dual-model oversight architecture introduces distinct failure modes that require defensive engineering mitigations.

| Failure Mode | Underlying Mechanism | Observable System Impact | Architectural Mitigation Strategy |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| **Hint-Induced Anchoring** | Overseer provides an incorrect or overly narrow localization hypothesis during plan review14. | Orchestrator restricts search to incorrect files; resolution rates plummet by up to 16.9%14. | Limit overseer plan critiques to negative constraints and invariant validation; prohibit speculative file localization14. |
| **Critic Hallucination & Nitpicking** | Overseer hallucinates non-existent syntax flaws or flags pedantic stylistic issues7. | Worker agent enters churn loops, breaking working implementations to satisfy false critiques7. | Enforce persistent notes with admission audits: critic must cite verifiable failing lines and executable test cases10. |
| **Compaction Cliff Amnesia** | Trajectory summarizer drops vital environment flags, mock data, or CLI execution parameters32. | Local worker repeatedly fails tool executions due to missing environmental parameters17. | Persist environment configurations in immutable system memory outside the compressible transcript32. |
| **Supervisor Creep / Takeover** | Overseer outputs complete code patches instead of diagnostic steering directions3. | Output token usage surges; system collapses economically into expensive monolithic execution3. | Enforce strict JSON output schemas; automatically reject and truncate overseer outputs containing code blocks3. |
| **Adherence-Resolution Disconnect** | Worker follows overseer instructions syntactically without fixing the root logical defect12. | Overseer assumes compliance solved the issue; circular debugging resumes12. | Decouple adherence checks (diff parsing) from resolution audits (independent executable test evaluation)12. |

To maintain analytical rigor, system designers must distinguish verified empirical research from vendor marketing claims. The effectiveness of hybrid event-triggered oversight, persistent note tracking, and typed critic operators is empirically established across peer-reviewed and preprint literature, notably by Mei et al. (*Opera*, arXiv:2609.33987, October 2026\) and Gandhi et al. (arXiv:2606.21811, June 2026\) across SWE-bench Verified, SWE-bench Pro, and Terminal-Bench 2.13. The mechanics of context degradation and the "Compaction Cliff" are validated by Compact-Bench (arXiv:2610.31710, late 2026\) and CompactionRL (arXiv:2607.05378)32.  
Conversely, promotional assertions claiming 32× harness cost reductions or fully autonomous monorepo migrations represent vendor-selected benchmarks conducted under narrow, proprietary scaffolding18. In production codebases featuring legacy dependencies and unmocked external services, autonomous issue resolution without human supervision remains bounded23. Systems operating in enterprise settings must maintain human-in-the-loop escalation paths for high-risk operations and rely on deterministic verification rather than unvalidated model claims23.

## **Structural Synthesis and Engineering Directives**

Implementing strong-model oversight over a local Qwen 3.x orchestrator requires separating execution authority from governance enforcement22. Reserving Claude Opus exclusively for high-leverage inflection points—specifically pre-commit completion claims, consecutive check failures, and high-risk domain modifications—maximizes defect interception while preserving a disciplined inference budget3.  
The governance topology must remain mechanical rather than conversational22. The strong model must never act as an advisory entity whose warnings can be dismissed by the local agent, nor should it become an expensive worker that synthesizes routine code3. By enforcing structural, binding gates through deterministic harness hooks, passing structured context packages, and restricting the overseer's output to typed diagnostic operators, this architecture achieves an optimal balance between local execution speed, frontier cognitive reasoning, and operational cost efficiency3.
